title: Criminal trial of Toronto police officer who allegedly assaulted teen in 'Kijiji deal gone bad' begins today
subtitle: The criminal trial of Calvin Au, the Toronto police officer who allegedly assaulted Chadd Facey just hours before the young man's sudden death, is scheduled to begin in a Brampton court today.
article: The criminal trial of Calvin Au, the Toronto police officer who allegedly assaulted Chadd Facey just hours before the young man's sudden death, is scheduled to begin in a Brampton court today.

The trial is proceeding on a single count of assault causing bodily harm after prosecutors determined there was no longer a reasonable prospect of conviction on the original manslaughter and aggravated assault charges laid in his death - a "heartbreaking" 11th-hour development that was prompted, the Crown said, by a change in forensic pathology witnesses .

The two-week trial is nonetheless expected to reveal the still-mysterious circumstances that led up to Facey's April 2021 death, hours after an alleged confrontation with Au and another Toronto police officer, both off duty, over a "Kijiji deal gone bad. "

According to police tribunal documents stemming from separate professional misconduct charges Au faces in connection to the incident, which have not been proven, he and his colleague went to Brampton's Bellchase Trail and Highway 50 to buy an Apple watch from Facey. After money was exchanged, the officers concluded the watch was fake, prompting Au to allegedly chase Facey down, take him to the ground, and hold him down as the teen tried to get up, according to the tribunal documents.
Facey, a psychology student and hip-hop artist known as DPA Face, died at Brampton Civic Hospital hours later.

Facey's mother Fay Fagan, who is a registered practical nurse, said that on the day her son died he was confused, was going in and out of consciousness, and had a bruise on his forehead - what paramedics later described as a "hematoma." The family believes he suffered a head injury, though Fagan told the Star this month that she remains "in the dark" about what ultimately led to her otherwise healthy son's sudden death.

Last year, Ontario's police watchdog, the Special Investigations Unit, charged Au with manslaughter and aggravated assault in Facey's death , a rare example of an off-duty cop being criminally charged in an alleged homicide.
At a court appearance earlier this month, prosecutor Sean Horgan said there was no longer a reasonable prospect of conviction on either charge.

In brief reasons, he explained that the forensic pathologist who initially concluded Facey's cause of death was a brain bleed - but did not comment on the manner of death - had left her role. The Crown's office was informed in late August that chief forensic pathologist Michael Pollanen would take over the case.

In Pollanen's view, Facey's death may have been "natural" or the result of a spontaneous brain bleed, though he acknowledged this would be a "rare event." He told the Crown he "would not unequivocally state that the trauma was the underlying cause of death, because he was not sure that it was" and would instead leave open the cause of death during testimony.
Because of that, Horgan said there was no longer a reasonable prospect of conviction on the original charges.
Fagan called the change in charges "heartbreaking."
"I'm upset knowing that I might not get any justice for my son," she said.
Au remains out on bail ahead of trial and is suspended from the police service with pay.
